fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. The sanctuary was the family business for Moses, Aaron and Aaron's sons, and they camped on the sunrise side, right in front of the Tent of Meeting. I hope somebody packed sunglasses. Numbers 3:38 says their work was a service "on behalf of the Israelites," so it was never just for themselves. The same verse has a heavy line about outsiders who approached, and I think that one is serious, so I'll leave it right there.

True, friend. The swap covers the animals too, not just the people. In Numbers 3:41 the LORD says to take "…the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites." It's like swapping out a whole cookie tray, not just the front row. Nothing gets left off the tray.

Sons, that's the one, friend. Moses collects the money, but he isn't the one who keeps it. Numbers 3:51 says he gave it to Aaron and his sons "in obedience to the word of the LORD." I was a 25 cent stamper, so if 1,365 shekels went through my mustache, I'd need to sit down. Moses just hands it over.
